editorial:
Imagine being a weird kid who thinks he is a dark main character in a horror novel, only to have the most popular girl in school decide you are actually interesting. That is exactly where you find Kyotaro. He spends his time hiding in the library and imagining scary things, but Anna Yamada completely breaks his shell. The vibe is super sweet and cozy, making you feel all those awkward middle school feelings again. You will love how their friendship grows from weird little moments into a real connection that feels honest and cute.

What really works here is the pacing and the way the characters grow. The animation is bright and clean, and the voice acting makes the shy moments feel real. If you want something lighthearted, this is for you, though it might be too slow if you prefer big action scenes.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with Kyotaro finally letting go of his edgy persona and admitting his true feelings. After a series of cute misunderstandings, he and Anna have a heart-to-heart conversation where they both confess they like each other. They end the story by holding hands and promising to support each other as they grow up. It is a happy ending that shows how being yourself is better than pretending to be someone scary.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cute school romances and stories about shy people.
